title: White Crown
subtitle: A marble love letter on the banks of the Yamuna

chapters.label: CHAPTER 01 · THE COMMISSION
chapters.heading: The emperor placed grief in ivory marble.
chapters.subheading: Shah Jahan ordered a monument in 1631.
chapters.body: Shah Jahan commissioned an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the Yamuna in Agra to house the tomb of his late wife Mumtaz Mahal. The project began in 1632 and the central tomb was finished in 1648, while the surrounding garden and buildings followed for another five years.

chapters.label: CHAPTER 02 · THE CRAFT
chapters.heading: Scaffolds of brick mirrored a marble sky.
chapters.subheading: Artisans from many lands built the complex.
chapters.body: More than 20,000 workers, artisans, sculptors, calligraphers and designers from regions including Bukhara, Persia, southern India, Baluchistan and Italy contributed. Marble came from Makrana in Rajasthan, red sandstone from Fatehpur Sikri, and 28 varieties of precious stone were inlaid. A 15 km earthen ramp and pulley systems moved the blocks into place.

chapters.label: CHAPTER 03 · THE VISIT
chapters.heading: A full-moon night opens the gates briefly.
chapters.subheading: The site draws millions each year.
chapters.body: About five million visitors visited the Taj Mahal in the financial year 2022-23. It is open from one hour before sunrise to 45 minutes before sunset, with limited night viewing on full-moon days. Vehicles are barred near the walls, so guests walk or take electric buses through three gates into the garden and towards the marble tomb.
